q: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower ____.
e: The diffusion of gases takes place from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Cell respiration uses oxygen and produces ____.
e: Cell respiration uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Plants require oxygen for respiration and carbon dioxide for ____.
e: Plants require oxygen for respiration and carbon dioxide for photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: The movement of gases in and out of green plants is via a process called ____.
e: The movement of gases in and out of green plants is via a process called diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on ____ for gas exchange.
e: Single-celled organisms and small and thin organisms rely on diffusion for gas exchange. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: In larger organisms, simple diffusion alone is not an efficient way of transporting gases between cells in the body and the gas exchange ____.
e: In larger organisms, simple diffusion alone is not an efficient way of transporting gases between cells in the body and the gas exchange surface. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: The rate of gas exchange is affected by: the area available for diffusion, the distance over which diffusion occurs, the concentration gradient across the gas exchange surface, and the speed with which molecules diffuse through ____.
e: The rate of gas exchange is affected by: the area available for diffusion, the distance over which diffusion occurs, the concentration gradient across the gas exchange surface, and the speed with which molecules diffuse through membranes. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: Efficient gas exchange systems must: have a large surface area to volume ratio, be thin, have mechanisms for maintaining steep concentration gradients across themselves, and be permeable to ____.
e: Efficient gas exchange systems must: have a large surface area to volume ratio, be thin, have mechanisms for maintaining steep concentration gradients across themselves, and be permeable to gases. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened.

q: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they will be taking in carbon dioxide and giving out ____.
e: In daylight, when photosynthesis is going on in green plants, they will be taking in carbon dioxide and giving out oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: When respiration is going on, they will be taking in oxygen and giving out ____.
e: When respiration is going on, they will be taking in oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the ____.
e: In plants, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse through the stomata and the lenticels. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases. Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through stomata.

q: The stomata are the openings in the epidermis of the plant especially of the ____.
e: The stomata are the openings in the epidermis of the plant especially of the leaves. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the ____ which contain the chloroplasts.
e: A stoma is bounded by a pair of specialized cells known as the guard cells which contain the chloroplasts. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: The stomata allow the gas exchange and ____.
e: The stomata allow the gas exchange and transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: Oxygen produced as a by-product of photosynthesis diffuses out to the atmosphere through these same ____.
e: Oxygen produced as a by-product of photosynthesis diffuses out to the atmosphere through these same openings. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: The guard cells are responsible for regulating the opening and closing of ____.
e: The guard cells are responsible for regulating the opening and closing of stomata. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the turgor pressure of the ____.
e: Stomatal opening and closing depends on changes in the turgor pressure of the guard cells. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells.

q: Normally the stomata are opened in the daytime and closed at ____.
e: Normally the stomata are opened in the daytime and closed at night. Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: In the daytime, when water diffuses into the guard cells by osmosis, their turgor increases and they ____.
e: In the daytime, when water diffuses into the guard cells by osmosis, their turgor increases and they expand. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor. Osmosis is diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane.

q: Due to the relatively inelastic inner wall, the guard cells bend and draw away from each other, so the pore ____.
e: Due to the relatively inelastic inner wall, the guard cells bend and draw away from each other, so the pore opens. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: If the guard cells lose water, the opposite happens and the pore ____.
e: If the guard cells lose water, the opposite happens and the pore closes. Guard cells open and close each stoma by changing turgor.

q: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and ____.
e: Lenticels are small openings on stems, fruits, tubers and roots. Roots may use air spaces or aerenchyma when soil oxygen is low. Lenticels are cork pores that let woody stems exchange gases.

q: Lenticel provides a pathway for the direct exchange of gases between the internal tissues and atmosphere through it, which is otherwise ____ to gases.
e: Lenticel provides a pathway for the direct exchange of gases between the internal tissues and atmosphere through it, which is otherwise impermeable to gases. The atmosphere is the layer of gases around the earth.

q: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood vessels surrounding the ____.
e: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place between the air and the blood vessels surrounding the alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin.

q: The two lungs contain about seven hundred millions of these tiny air sacs, giving a total surface area of ____.
e: The two lungs contain about seven hundred millions of these tiny air sacs, giving a total surface area of 60m². A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only two cell layers: the cells making up the wall of the alveolus, and the ____ itself.
e: The blood is separated from the air inside each alveolus by only two cell layers: the cells making up the wall of the alveolus, and the capillary wall itself. Each alveolus is a thin-walled sac where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: This is a distance of less than a thousandth of a millimeter, which provides short diffusion distance for oxygen and ____.
e: This is a distance of less than a thousandth of a millimeter, which provides short diffusion distance for oxygen and carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: In plants, transport of gases is only by simple ____.
e: In plants, transport of gases is only by simple diffusion. Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration.

q: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the ____.
e: In humans, deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary artery. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from heart to lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the ____, which returns blood to the left atrium of the heart.
e: The capillaries carrying oxygenated blood from the alveoli join up to form the pulmonary vein, which returns blood to the left atrium of the heart. The pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from lungs to the heart. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens.

q: In fish, the oxygenated blood is distributed to the respiring tissues all over the body directly from the ____.
e: In fish, the oxygenated blood is distributed to the respiring tissues all over the body directly from the gills. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces.

q: In insects, the tracheoles which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every ____.
e: In insects, the tracheoles which are the finest branches extend close to the surface of nearly every cell. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Insect tracheoles take air almost to the tissues, so blood need not carry the gases.
